summary: A notice that UCLA's Network Measurement Center would gather NCP statistics from hosts automatically each day. It opens a connection to a local socket 241 and expects counts such as bits and messages sent and received, plus optional round-trip delay. Results would be published monthly.

plainLanguage.summary: A school will call each computer every day and ask how much it sent and received, then share a report each month.

subtitle: UCLA offers to collect daily NCP traffic counts from each ARPANET host over socket 241.

tldr.problem: Network measurement needed regular traffic statistics from each host's NCP, and the earlier request in RFC 323 had lapsed for 5 months.
tldr.mechanism: UCLA-NMC periodically opens a connection to socket 241 on each participating host, which sends a binary report of bits, messages and optional delay, per foreign host, for the last 24 hours.
tldr.outcome: Results were to be published monthly as Network Measurement notes and RFCs. UCLA-NMC, DMCG and LL-67 were the participants named.

today: RFC 388 is listed as updating RFC 323, and its status is Unknown. It describes a 1972 measurement arrangement and is not listed as replaced.

sections.title: The Daily Collection Offer
sections.content:
Vint Cerf of UCLA-NMC announces, after a 5 month lapse since RFC 323 (23 March), that the center is ready to gather NCP statistics automatically each day. The unit metadata lists this RFC as updating RFC 323.

UCLA-NMC will periodically open a connection on the host's local socket 241 (decimal) and expect the host to send its data as soon as the Allocate command arrives. This replaces the original idea of an ICP to a well-known socket, which Cerf considers an unnecessary complication. The host closes the connection after it receives the RFNM for its last message.
sections.plainLanguage: UCLA will ring a special doorbell on each computer once a day. The computer then hands over its numbers.

sections.title: What Is Counted
sections.content:
For each host, the counts are total bits sent to and received from the host, total messages sent to and received from the host, and optionally the average round trip delay on send connections. Only standard open connections count, not measurement links or experimental NCP links, and not traffic on link 0; data is for open connections on links 0, 2-71 as the RFC phrases it.

An optional extra is the distribution of message types over link 0 across all hosts, which would show the relative use of control messages. The RFC expects ALLOC to be very prevalent. The figures cover the local 24 hour day, midnight to midnight, not a sliding window.
sections.plainLanguage: The computer reports how many bits and messages went in and out for each partner computer. It does not count the special test traffic.

sections.title: The Report Format
sections.content:
Word 0 holds a 16 bit day number (1 to 365, 6 on leap year) and a 16 bit time in minutes from 0 to 1439 at which sampling began. Word 1 holds the source host (8 bits), byte size (8 bits), N, the number of host related entries, and a format byte. Format flag bits C, R, B and M say whether control message distribution, average delay, byte statistics and message statistics are present.

Then come N entries, each starting with the foreign host number and followed by the counts that the format bits select. The optional control message distribution is a list of 8 bit type and 24 bit count pairs; a missing type counts as 0. Average delay is the average RFNM delay in milliseconds.
sections.plainLanguage: The report is a form with boxes. The first boxes say the date and who is reporting, and the rest list the numbers for each partner computer.

sections.title: Participation
sections.content: Anyone can connect to UCLA-NMC socket 241 to receive its own 24 hour data and is welcome to capture it. The named participants are UCLA-NMC, DMCG and LL-67, and other hosts are heartily invited to join. Results were to be published monthly as Network Measurement notes and RFCs.
sections.plainLanguage: Anyone can ask UCLA for its numbers too. Three groups had signed up, and others were invited.

viz.caption: FIRST TWO WORDS OF THE REPORT (RFC 388)

fields.name: Day #
fields.desc: Day of year, 1 to 365 (6 on leap year).

fields.name: Time
fields.desc: Minutes at which the sample started, 0 to 1439.

fields.name: Source Host
fields.desc: Network host number of the reporter.

fields.name: Byte Size
fields.desc: Bits per byte in byte statistics.

fields.name: Format
fields.desc: Flag bits C, R, B and M select the optional contents.

references.text: RFC 323, the earlier request for NCP statistics, issued 23 March 1972.
